reason: The claimed +0.004 is not reachable, and even a perfect fix stays below the +0.002 gate. (1) Value per edge, from per_video_all.csv exp39 weighted by GT edge count: turning one FN into a TP is worth 7.05e-6 (G = 128,883 GT edges). Recomputed from fn_exp39.parquet and the TP edges: the six boundary edge slots (t = 0,1,2 and 96,97,98) have 77/84/88 and 68/70/96 FN, which is 7.8-8.1% and 6.0/6.4/9.0% vs 5.1% in the middle. That is 483 FN on 6,398 GT edges, of which only 157 are in excess of the middle-frame rate. The oracle ceiling is 157 x 7.05e-6 = +0.0011, with zero node or FP cost. Recovering ALL 483 boundary FN, including the normal baseline, would give only +0.0034, still below the claimed +0.004. The hypothesis double-counts: '236 unmatched nodes x 2 edges' ignores that nodes at t=0 and t=T-1 have one in-clip edge and that neighbouring missing nodes share edges. Its extra '+0.0009 a_tail' is already inside the 157 (a_tail is ~111 of the excess). (2) Node multiplier, measured exactly: final Npred 4.131M, Nest 4.725M. The marginal cost of one added node, weighted by GT edges and J, is 2.13e-8 overall (3.55e-8 on 6bba, 0.58e-8 on 44b6), so +1% nodes everywhere costs -0.00088. Break-even precision: an added node must carry >= 0.003 recovered TP edges (0.005 on 6bba). The final graph has a clip-end node deficit of about 50k nodes (t0 0.784, t99 0.706 of the mid mean; ~26k missing at the start and ~24k at the end). Restoring them all costs 50k x 2.13e-8 = -0.0011, exactly the +0.0011 edge ceiling: the missing boundary nodes as a whole carry ~0.003 TP/node, which is break-even. Only targeted restoration can be positive. (3) Realistic capture per sub-change. Tail rule (b), K=4: start 66 FN / 11.8k nodes gives +4.7e-4 - 2.5e-4 = +2.1e-4; end 55 FN / 11.3k nodes gives +3.9e-4 - 2.4e-4 = +1.5e-4. That is about +3.6e-4 before FP edges; at the short-component FP:TP ratio (~0.14 x 6.4e-6 per FP) about +3e-4 net. The research note's node cost used a 2.11M node base and is about 2x too high, so (b) is slightly positive, not negative, but tiny. ILP clip-end exemption: 118 excess a_never x 7.05e-6 = +8.3e-4 minus 12.6k nodes x 2.13e-8 = 2.7e-4, i.e. +5.6e-4 at 100% capture if every restored segment survives the short-track filter; at a realistic 40-60% capture, +2e-4 to +3e-4. Divisions: 5 of 151 GT parents lie near the ends; +1 division TP = 0.1 x 1/194 = +5e-4, a lottery with an expected value near 0. Combined realistic local gain: +0.0003 to +0.0007; public 0 to +0.0004. That is below the LB's 0.001 resolution and less than 3% of the +0.022 needed for 0.97. (4) Protocol: the gains sit in few videos (121 reachable tail FN across 199 videos), while the node cost hits every video. So the >= 55% per-embryo win-rate criterion very likely fails, as it did for stitch, and the +0.002 gate is above the oracle.
fix_if_any: Drop part (a); the research found no padding, the detector is permutation-equivariant. Treat (b) plus the ILP exemption as a free add-on, not a standalone idea. Measure it under a relaxed criterion (net > 0 on confirmation with CI > 0; the win-rate test is waived because most videos are untouched). Maximise precision instead of recall: keep only boundary-touching components of 4-5 nodes that have mean edge_prob >= 0.8 AND lie within 7 um of no existing long track (to avoid duplicates that steal links). Only then does the per-node TP rate exceed the 0.003-0.005 break-even by a margin. Bundle the ILP exemption (disappearance C_END ~0.05-0.5 at t=T-1, appearance bonus ~0.5-1 at t=0) into any future Kaggle pass that already dumps the pre-ILP candidate graph for another idea; never spend a dedicated GPU run or an LB probe on it. Expected ceiling after repair: about +0.0005 local.
realistic_public_gain: 0 to +0.0004 (local +0.0003 to +0.0007; the oracle ceiling is +0.0011 local before node cost). Not detectable on the 3-decimal public LB, and not a route to 0.97.
